title: Who slept well?
hookLine: "I slept well": a breakfast sentence becomes Ramanuja's evidence that the self is a real someone
carry: the atman is a real someone, a lamp with light

cards: Breakfast. Someone asks how you slept, and you say, I slept well. Simple.
But stop on it for a second. In deep sleep you weren't thinking, weren't dreaming, weren't aware of the room. So who slept well?
And how does that someone know? Ramanuja uses exactly this ordinary sentence in the Sri Bhashya, in a long argument about what consciousness is, and whether there's a someone inside it.
The breakfast table, it turns out, is a good place to do theology.

teach.b: Advaita teachers, in Shankara's line, say the deepest reality is pure consciousness, with no owner and no object, and that the sense of I is laid over it, like a snake seen on a rope.
Ramanuja sets that view out at length, then answers it. Every awareness, he says, has two features: it belongs to someone, and it shows something. I know the cup.
I see the light. Awareness with no knower and nothing known isn't anything anyone has met. Then the breakfast line.
On waking and saying I slept well, he argues, the I was there all along; it simply wasn't knowing much.
So the self, the atman, is a real knower, not a mask over knowing. To hold both, he uses a lamp.
A lamp is bright in itself, and it also has light that spreads out from it into the room. The light is real, and it's the lamp's.
In the same way, the self is conscious by nature, and it has consciousness that reaches out toward things.
In bondage that reach is narrowed, like light behind a shutter. In freedom it opens wide. Advaita teachers answer him in turn, and both schools keep reading.
For Ramanuja, this is what the atman is: a real someone in your awareness, real enough to love God and to be loved by him.

how: Sri Vaishnava students meet this argument in the Sri Bhashya's long opening section, studied with a teacher, where Ramanuja sets out the Advaita view in full and answers it; Advaita students study the replies made from their side.

o: careful thought about Vishnu, the self and the world

games.q: you wake up and say, I slept well. you're Ramanuja. what does that sentence show you?
o: that the I was there through deep sleep.
that nobody was there at all.
games.why: Ramanuja argues the I persists through deep sleep: a real knower that simply wasn't knowing much.

practice: Rest your attention on one sound in the room, and notice both that there's a sound and that it's being heard. Then let attention widen, the way light spreads, to every sound at once, and narrow it again to one.
Through all of it, notice the one who is noticing; if you pray, rest that noticing in the name you pray to.

wordCard.voice: Vaishnava theology. Today, Ramanuja's lamp: the atman, a self that is conscious by nature, with a light of awareness that narrows and opens wide.

orig.note: Sanskrit: attributive consciousness, the self's light of awareness in Ramanuja's school.

carryVoice: Your line: the atman is a real someone, a lamp with its light. Someone slept well, and someone woke up to say so. Same time tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ramanuja, Sri Bhashya 1.1.1 (the great prior view and its answer: consciousness has a knower and an object; deep sleep; the lamp and its light)
